TAP ZONE TEST (justify). This paragraph is deliberately long, to take several lines and stretch across the width: it is on stretched lines that the offset between the drawn footnote number and its tap zone becomes noticeable, because justify adds width only when drawing, not in the layout geometry. Somewhere around here, near the right edge of one of the INNER lines, stands the footnote marker[5], and after it some more text follows on purpose, so that this line is full (justified) rather than the last one of the paragraph. EXPECTED: with justified alignment on, a tap exactly on the visible “[5]” opens the note instead of toggling the reader menu. If “[5]” landed on the first or last line, change the font size or the orientation so that it becomes an inner one.

The author's punctuation must reach the reader unchanged. Before the #28 fix the parser cut every “*” and “_” out of the text, its own along with the author's.
20.1. Asterisk footnote: (*) — the asterisk in parentheses must be visible.
20.2. Numbered footnote: a month passed after the event (*1) — “(*1)” intact.
20.3. Two numbered ones in one paragraph: footnotes (*1) and (*2) — both intact, because a closing asterisk before a digit cannot close emphasis.
20.4. Underscores in a URL: https://example.org/wiki/Some_Long_Title_With_Underscores — every “_” in place.
20.5. Underscores inside a word: snake_case_identifier — “_” in place.
20.6. A lone underscore in parentheses: (_) — must be visible.
20.7. Spaces around bold text — the words must not run together.

20.8. Private-use characters the book brought itself, from the block the parser once used for its own marks:  — and the Apple logo, U+F8FF: . They must NOT switch on italic, bold or strike-through. As of #29 the first ones are shown as they are, like any other character the book holds.

20.9. KNOWN LIMIT: two bare asterisks in parentheses, both surrounded by punctuation, are an emphasis pair to CommonMark. The next line is the only one in this section where the characters DISAPPEAR and the text between them turns italic. Not a regression; only the move to a DOM walk (#29) cures it.
See (*) and also (*).
EXPECTED: nothing lost in 20.1–20.8; only the line under 20.9 shows a loss.
These are not FB2 tags — this is how EPUB and HTML write them, and they go through the same parser. Added in #31, kept here because this book is the easiest place to check them.

title.p: 22. An illustration at the end of a chapter (#75)

section.p: This section ends with an image — chapter 23 starts right after it, with no paragraph in between. This is where the chapter break lives: the empty space under the picture belongs to the break, not to the picture.

EXPECTED: a tap on the empty space under the image does NOT open the image viewer — it means the same as a tap on the page (paging at the edges, the menu in the middle). A tap on the picture itself opens it, as before.

title.p: 23. A chapter right after an illustration

section.p: This chapter's title has a larger margin above than below it — that is how the reader sees that the previous chapter has ended.
End of section 23.

This is a deliberately large note for checking scrolling in the popup. Its text purposely does not fit on one screen, so the bottom panel must scroll, and the formatting must survive in every paragraph.

Paragraph 1. Here we check that an empty line stays between paragraphs, and that a line break inside a paragraph is folded by the reader into one continuous flow of words without stray breaks in unexpected places.
Paragraph 2. Formatting inside a note: a bold fragment, an italic fragment and a struck-through fragment must be rendered, not shown as markup characters.
Paragraph 3. Indices must work too: the formula H2O with a subscript “2” and xn with a superscript exponent must look right even inside a note.
Paragraph 4. Filler with no meaning, only to add height: line after line, sentence after sentence, until the total length surely exceeds the screen height and makes the panel scroll.
Paragraph 5. One more paragraph of the same kind. The goal is simple — make sure no fragment of text is cut off at the bottom and that scrolling reaches the very end of the content.
Paragraph 6. A check that long paragraphs wrap by words on their own and do not run past the panel horizontally, even when the text contains long-long-long compound words.
Paragraph 7. An intermediate paragraph, to be sure to go past one screen even on a large tablet in landscape, where noticeably more lines fit on a screen.
Paragraph 8. A little more text for height. If this paragraph is visible only after scrolling, that is already a good sign the mechanism works as it should.
Paragraph 9. The second to last paragraph. Next comes one final paragraph with an explicit end marker, visible only if the note is scrolled all the way down.
🔚 Paragraph 10 (THE END). If you can see this line, scrolling of a large note works to the end, and no paragraph got lost.
Text of the seventh note — the footnote in the TITLE of section 16 points to it.
